newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian PM defends meeting Dalai Lama.
newsitem.headline: Australian PM defends meeting Dalai Lama.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard, shrugging off a warning from China, on Wednesday defended his decision to meet Tibet's exiled spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, who is on a two-week visit to Australia.
Howard told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio in Indonesia, where is on a visit, that it would be strange if he shunned such an important religious leader.
"He is a significant religious leader and it's appropriate in those circumstances, as he's a guest in Australia, that I see him," Howard said.
"It would be strange if I didn't, and I don't think the Australian people would expect me to spurn an invitation to meet him as a significant religious leader."

Beijing,, which views the Dalai Lama as a political activist out to split China, issued a warning on Tuesday that foreign leaders who meet the Tibetan leader would see trade and business ties with China suffer.
The Dalai Lama has been in exile since an abortive uprising against Chinese rule in Tibet in 1959. He won the 1989 Nobel Peace Prize for his peaceful campaign for Tibetan autonomy.
Howard hopes to meet the Dalai Lama in Sydney next week if their programmes allow.
Howard would not comment on Beijing's threats.
"I don't want to over-react to it. I note what a spokesman for the foreign ministry has said and I'm not going to take it any further," he said.
"I've discussed the matter with the Chinese ambassador, he understands our position," Howard said.
"We value that relationship and we'll continue to work on it," he said.
The Dalai Lama started his visit to Australia last Saturday. He has met Foreign Minister Alexander Downer for unofficial talks and met several politicians in Canberra on Tuesday.
